City council approves the new riverside park

By Jane Rivers

18 April 2024
Share on Social Email this story

The city council voted on Tuesday evening to approve plans for a twelve-hectare park along the eastern bank of the river, ending a debate that has lasted for almost a decade.

Councillors said the park would turn a stretch of disused warehouses into green space for more than forty thousand residents who currently live more than a kilometre away from any public garden.

“This is the most important decision this council has made in a generation,” said the council leader, adding that construction could begin as early as next spring, subject to a final review.

We have waited a long time for this, and the whole neighbourhood will benefit from it for decades to come.

What happens next

The project will now go to a public consultation, which runs for twelve weeks. Residents can comment on the design, the opening hours and the plans for lighting along the river path.

  • Consultation opens in May and closes at the end of July.
  • Final designs are expected in the autumn, after the review.

Opponents had argued that the land should be used for housing, but a compromise agreed last month sets aside a third of the site for affordable homes along the northern edge, which won the support of both main groups on the council.

Comments

Finally! I have been writing to the council about this park for years, and I am so glad that they have listened to the residents of the eastern bank at last.

I am not convinced. The housing shortage in this city is severe and we need homes more than we need another park, however pretty the drawings look.

Will there be enough parking? Every new attraction in this city brings more traffic to streets that are already completely congested on weekends.
